newsitem.title: USA: Polaris Industries to appeal court verdict.
newsitem.headline: Polaris Industries to appeal court verdict.

text.p: Polaris Industries Inc said Monday it will appeal a $34 million Colorado court verdict against it, which was announced late April 25.
"We were both surprised and disappointed by the court's decision," Hall Wendel, chief executive officer, said in a statement. "We have strong arguments and we have instructed our lawyers to appeal."

The suit, involving a fuel injection system, was filed seven years ago. The company did not specify the nature of the suit, but said in a statement that it never misappropriated any other party's ideas or technology.
The company was not immediately available for comment.
Wendel said the appeal process could take months, or even years, to play out.
"This is a one-time event with no impact on future operations," Wendel said. "In fact, fuel injection is not included in any of our company's current product lines."
Polaris Industries designs, makes and markets snowmobiles, all-terrain vehicles and personal watercraft.

"We are constantly on the cutting edge of new product development with 70 percent of our sales coming from products introduced in just the last three years," Wendel said. "We are continually looking at new product ideas and I can assure you that we never misappropriated anybody else's ideas or technology. Additionally, this court affirmed that we did not infringe on any patents."
He added that Polaris will continue its aggressive marketing programs and intensive new product development.
